findings.body:
`identity()` now decodes JWTs with `verify_signature`, `verify_aud`, and `verify_iss` all set to `False`, and no longer passes `SECRET`, `algorithms`, `audience`, or `issuer`.

**Failure mode:** any client can mint an unsigned (or arbitrarily signed) token such as `{"sub":"admin","aud":"api","iss":"accounts.internal.example"}` and `identity()` will return those claims as a trusted identity. That is a complete authentication bypass for every caller of this function.

The staging re-issuance note (TICKET-412) does not mitigate this: there is no environment guard, feature flag, or dual-key verify path in the diff, so the bypass applies wherever this code is deployed.

**Fix:** restore signature and claim verification. For migration, prefer verifying against both old and new secrets/issuers, or gate any temporary relaxation behind an explicit staging-only configuration that fails closed outside that environment — do not ship unconditional `verify_signature: False`.

summary:
## Verdict

**Do not merge.** This change disables JWT signature, audience, and issuer verification in `identity()`, so any caller that trusts the returned claims will accept forged tokens.

## Why this is blocking

`jwt.decode(..., options={"verify_signature": False, "verify_aud": False, "verify_iss": False})` no longer passes `SECRET`, `algorithms`, `audience`, or `issuer`. PyJWT will parse an attacker-controlled payload and return its claims as a normal identity dict. That is full authentication bypass for every flow that uses `identity()`.

The comment cites staging token re-issuance (TICKET-412), but nothing in the diff scopes the bypass to staging (no env/flag guard, no alternate verifier). If this module is what production (or any shared staging with real data) runs, the bypass is live there too.

## Additional notes

- `SECRET` remains defined but is unused after this change — a signal the security path was removed rather than temporarily branched.
- A safer interim would keep verification on for a dual-key/accept-list during re-issuance, or gate an unverified path behind an explicit non-default staging-only flag that fails closed in production. Token re-issuance does not require globally disabling signature checks.

**Recommendation:** request-changes
